header.name: Political Concepts in Contemporary India
header.description: The course equips students to think analytically about contemporary digital political life and community-making through key concepts in contemporary political theory. Whereas the terminology and the language of these concepts are shaped historically and have a universal meaning, the digital turn in political processes necessitates a renewed imagination of these concepts. The course will demonstrate how concepts embody particular systems of meanings, and will enable students to critique the historical, empirical and normative dimensions of political life in contemporary India. Through the course, the students will also be able to develop an analytical criterion to evaluate the politics of the state and the state of politics in the digital era. Divided into three main parts, the course  enables students to develop a theoretical understanding of an individual, conceptualise the political community, and enable them to analyze the relationship between the two. The course is relevant both at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels. At the undergraduate level, it enables students to develop contextual critique. For graduate students, especially in the social sciences, it serves as a course on the state of the field in political theory.
prerequisites_desirable: SOC101: Introduction to Sociology and Anthropology

outcomes.label: CO1

outcomes.label: CO4
